# row space of a matrix　`def.row-space`
English entry · root `../`
[in graph](../#n=def.row-space)　·　[Chinese page (authoritative)](./def.row-space.md)

is the **row space** of $A$, and its dimension is the **row rank**. Equivalently, $\operatorname{Row}(A) = \operatorname{Col}(A^{\mathsf T})$, the column space of $A^{\mathsf T}$.

**Elementary row operations preserve the row space**: left multiplication by an invertible matrix only replaces the row vectors by another basis (row operations replace the rows by invertible linear combinations of them), so row-equivalent matrices have the same row space. Hence the nonzero rows of a row echelon form give a basis of $\operatorname{Row}(A)$.
